instruction: CDN paths are case-sensitive: use three.min.js exactly
input: An app loaded https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/Three.js and every THREE.* call failed with 'THREE is not defined'. Why, and what is the correct URL?
output:
The file at cdnjs is literally named three.min.js (lowercase). A capital-T 'Three.js' URL 404s, so THREE never loads and every THREE.* reference throws. Use exactly:
https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js

instruction: Fix the 3D solar system app (THREE.OrbitPath crash)
input: The app crashed with 'THREE.OrbitPath is not a constructor'. OrbitPath is not a real Three.js class. Fix it: load OrbitControls from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js, create controls with new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement), draw orbit rings with THREE.Line + BufferGeometry.setFromPoints of cos/sin points, store each planet's {distance, speed, angle} in userData, and advance angle in the animate loop.
output:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
	<meta charset="UTF-8">
	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
	<title>3D Solar System</title>
	<style>
		body { margin: 0; overflow: hidden; background: #000; }
		#canvas { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
	</style>
</head>
<body>
	<canvas id="canvas"></canvas>
	<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js"></script>
	<script>
		const scene = new THREE.Scene();
		const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 1000);
		const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true });
		renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
		document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
		camera.position.set(0, 0, 100);
		const controls = new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement);
		controls.enableDamping = true;
		controls.dampingFactor = 0.05;
		scene.add(new THREE.AxesHelper(10));
		const planets = [];
		function addPlanet(name, color, radius, distance, speed) {
			const geometry = new THREE.SphereGeometry(radius, 32, 32);
			const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color, flatShading: true });
			const planet = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
			const orbit = new THREE.Line(
				new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(
					Array.from({ length: 64 }, (_, i) => {
						const a = (i / 64) * Math.PI * 2;
						return new THREE.Vector3(Math.cos(a) * distance, 0, Math.sin(a) * distance);
					})),
				new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0x334466, transparent: true, opacity: 0.5 })
			);
			scene.add(orbit);
			planet.userData = { distance, speed, angle: Math.random() * Math.PI * 2 };
			planet.position.x = distance * Math.cos(planet.userData.angle);
			planet.position.y = 0;
			planet.position.z = distance * Math.sin(planet.userData.angle);
			scene.add(planet);
			planets.push(planet);
			return planet;
		}
		const sun = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(5, 32, 32), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xffffd5, emissive: 0xaaaaaa, roughness: 0.2, metalness: 0.8 }));
		sun.castShadow = true;
		scene.add(sun);
		const saturn = addPlanet('Saturn', 0x0080ff, 1, 15, 0.01);
		const rings = [];
		for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
			const ring = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.TorusGeometry(5, 0.5, 32, 32), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x80ff80, flatShading: true }));
			ring.position.x = 14.5;
			ring.position.z = 0.5 * (2 * i - 1);
			rings.push(ring);
			scene.add(ring);
		}
		function animate() {
			requestAnimationFrame(animate);
			sun.rotation.y += 0.005;
			planets.forEach(p => {
				p.userData.angle += 0.002 * p.userData.speed;
				p.position.x = p.userData.distance * Math.cos(p.userData.angle);
				p.position.z = p.userData.distance * Math.sin(p.userData.angle);
			});
			controls.update();
			renderer.render(scene, camera);
		}
		animate();
	</script>
</body>
</html>

instruction: Implement chess rules with check detection
input: Plain JavaScript chess rules: 8x8 board state, per-piece pseudo-legal moves with capture/en-passant/double-pawn flags, isAttacked with sliding-piece + knight + pawn attack checks, legal moves filtered by king safety (apply/undo), castling rights, auto-queen promotion, and a depth-2 minimax with material evaluation for the AI. Critical: applyMove must save the captured piece (mv.capture flag) so undoMove restores it — otherwise minimax corrupts the board.

Single-file HTML, Three.js r128 via CDN. Procedural terrain: PlaneGeometry(SIZE=26, SEGS=96) rotated -PI/2, vertices displaced by fractal value noise. Seeded noise (seed * 1103515245 + 12345 LCG) with smoothstep interpolation, fbm of 6 octaves halving amplitude and doubling frequency, per-octave seeds. Color the terrain by height bands (deep/shallow water, sand, grass, rock, snow) via vertex colors or colormap. Flat water plane at sea level with translucent blue material + wave-ish opacity. Controls: roughness slider (regenerates with new octave amplitude), wireframe toggle, randomize button. OrbitControls, sun DirectionalLight with shadows, starfield Points. HUD legend showing the color bands.

instruction: QA rule: never create hundreds of thousands of objects — use InstancedMesh and few lights
input: An app built a city with nested loops over a 1000x1000 grid creating ~110k Box meshes and ~200k PointLights, then the browser tab crashed. What is the right approach?
output: Per-object Meshes and especially PointLights are expensive: a scene with 100k+ objects or thousands of lights will freeze or crash the GPU/software renderer. For repeated geometry use ONE InstancedMesh with per-instance transforms (setMatrixAt), and light the whole scene with 1-3 lights (ambient + a sun/directional or spotlight). Never add a light inside a build loop.

input: Single-file HTML, Three.js r128 via CDN. Ball-and-stick molecule viewer: atom data (element, x,y,z) with per-element color + radius (C/H/O/N), bonds as cylinders scaled/oriented via quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(up, dir) between atom pairs. Three molecules: Water, Methane, Benzene (12 atoms, ring). Cycle button swaps molecules and updates the HUD caption; old meshes disposed. Slow group rotation. HemisphereLight + key light with shadows. OrbitControls, resize.

Three.js r128. Blobby organic motion from a sphere/icosahedron: scale.setScalar(0.85 + sin(t*s + ph)*0.28) + slow rotation on two axes + position.y = sin(t*spd + ph)*range. Cheap and convincing. Transparent emissive material sells the 'glowing liquid' look.
